title: Binary Tree Preorder Traversal
prompt:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the values of its nodes in pre-order traversal order (node, then left subtree, then right subtree).

The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it, so you only need to implement the traversal.

examples.explanation: Visit 1 first, then its right subtree, which visits 2 before its left child 3.
An empty tree has no nodes to visit, so the traversal result is an empty list.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 100]
hints: Pre-order means: visit the current node first, then fully traverse the left subtree, then fully traverse the right subtree.
An iterative solution can use an explicit stack: push the root, then repeatedly pop a node, record its value, and push its right child before its left child (so left is processed first).
Pushing right before left is the key trick — since a stack is LIFO, this guarantees the left subtree gets popped and visited before the right one.

solution.approach: Use an explicit stack starting with the root. Repeatedly pop a node, record its value, then push its right child followed by its left child (if they exist) — pushing right first ensures left comes off the stack first, preserving the node-left-right visiting order without recursion.
